root_cause.text: In `d_namespace_path()` in `security/apparmor/path.c`, after writing a `'/'` character to the buffer at `aa_g_path_max - 2` for directory paths, the null terminator at `aa_g_path_max - 1` was missing, leaving the string unterminated and causing an out-of-bounds read when passed to `aa_dfa_match()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `buf[aa_g_path_max - 1] = '\0';` after the line `buf[aa_g_path_max - 2] = '/';`, explicitly fixing the missing termination. The commit message states: "This was introduced by previous incorrect conversion from strcpy(). Fix it by adding the missing terminator." The KASAN report shows a slab-out-of-bounds read in `aa_dfa_match` at `match.c:535`, triggered via `match_mnt_path_str` from mount handling, confirming the unterminated string leads to a read beyond the allocated buffer.
